nodes.title: From the pro-Kummer-étale site of S^tor_{K,Σ} to the v-site of the toroidal tower diamond
nodes.statement: In the situation of S0.general/toroidal-tower-diamond, put X = S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ} with its fs log structure along the boundary and X_{K′_p} = S^tor_{K^pK′_p,Σ} for open normal K′_p ⊆ K_p. (i) Each X_{K′_p} → X is a finite Kummer étale Galois cover for the effective deck group K_p/(K′_p(K_p ∩ Z_K)), where Z_K is the closure in G(ℚ_p) of the arithmetic centre Z(ℚ) ∩ K; hence X̃_∞ := “lim” X_{K′_p} is an object of X_prokét and a pro-finite Kummer étale torsor under K_p/(K_p ∩ Z_K). (ii) For every log affinoid perfectoid object V of X_prokét over X̃_∞, its associated affinoid perfectoid space V̂ carries a canonical map V̂^◇ → S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞} = lim_{K′_p}(X_{K′_p})^◇, functorial in V. (iii) If {U_a → X} is a covering of X_prokét by log affinoid perfectoid objects, then V_a := U_a ×_X X̃_∞ is log affinoid perfectoid and a finite subfamily of the V̂_a^◇ → S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞} form a v-cover. (iv) For V, W log affinoid perfectoid over X̃_∞, the open subset of V̂^◇ ×_{S^{tor◇}} Ŵ^◇ lying over the open Shimura variety S_K is dense in |V̂^◇ ×_{S^{tor◇}} Ŵ^◇|. Consequently, maps V̂^◇ → Y to a separated v-sheaf Y that agree over S_K on all such fibre products descend uniquely to S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞}.
hypotheses: (G, X) a pure Shimura datum, K = K^pK_p neat, Σ a projective K-admissible cone decomposition, with the notation of S0.general/toroidal-tower-diamond; C complete algebraically closed over the reflex field.

Boxer–Pilloni state Theorem 4.4.40 and describe its evaluation on perfectoid tests (§4.6.1) without proving this comparison; RT-AREA-padic-1/4 and HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:comparison/hodge-tate-parabolic-reduction assign it to S6.
Part (iv) is conditional on the openness statement recorded in the gap 'Openness of the completed log affinoid perfectoid charts over the toroidal tower diamond'; (i)–(iii) do not use that input.
proofSteps: (i) The finite toroidal level maps for a fixed admissible Σ are log étale and Kummer along the boundary (in the cone charts the level change replaces the cusp lattice by a sublattice of finite index), hence finite Kummer étale (ShimuraCompactifications:C3.general/general-map-descent, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:log-sites/kummer-etale-morphism); they are Galois for the effective deck group because Z(ℚ) ∩ K acts trivially on the tower and the interior covers are Galois with this group (S0/tower-action-kernel), and a finite Kummer étale cover is determined by its restriction to the interior (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:log-sites/boundary-local-system-extension). The limit is pro-finite Kummer étale (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:log-sites/pro-kummer-etale-site).

(ii) A presentation V = lim V_i with V_i → X_{K′_p} for cofinal K′_p gives V̂ → V_i → X_{K′_p} on underlying adic spaces, compatible in K′_p; the diamond functor and the universal property of the limit give V̂^◇ → S^{tor◇} (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamonds-are-v-sheaves).

(iii) First choose finitely many U_a covering X: X is quasi-compact and X_prokét has the supplier’s quasi-compactness property for its actual transfinite-tower coverings (pro-kummer-etale-site, DLLZ Proposition 5.1.5), not merely arbitrary jointly surjective families. Then U_a ×_X X̃_∞ is a cofiltered limit of pullbacks of finite Kummer étale maps to the log affinoid perfectoid U_a, hence log affinoid perfectoid with V̂_a = lim of finite étale covers of Û_a (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:log-sites/log-perfectoid-basis (1), (3)). Points: a point of |S^{tor◇}| = lim |X_{K′_p}| (S0.general/toroidal-tower-diamond) is a compatible family (x_{K′_p}); choose a and a point u of |Û_a| over x_{K_p} (the U_a cover X). By the four-point lemma for the exact map X_{K′_p} → X (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:log-sites/saturated-adic-products (3)), the set of points of the fs fibre product U_a ×_X X_{K′_p} over (u, x_{K′_p}) is nonempty; these sets are compact in the constructible topology and form an inverse system in K′_p, so they have a compatible family, which is a point of |V̂_a| = lim_{K′_p} |U_a ×_X X_{K′_p}| (log-affinoid-perfectoid) over the given point. Hence the V̂_a^◇ jointly surject onto |S^{tor◇}|. The chosen finite subfamily still jointly surjects by this lifting argument. Its disjoint union is affinoid perfectoid componentwise and quasi-compact; the spatial target is quasi-separated, so the map is quasi-compact; a quasi-compact map of small v-sheaves that is surjective on points is a v-cover (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/isomorphism-criteria-for-v-sheaves-and-stacks).

(iv) The boundary of V̂ is the vanishing locus of the chart monomials, all of whose roots exist, so its complement is dense in |V̂|. If the projection V̂^◇ ×_{S^{tor◇}} Ŵ^◇ → V̂^◇ is open (the recorded gap: openness of Ŵ^◇ → S^{tor◇}, a limit of composites of Kummer étale maps, which are open on underlying spaces by HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:log-sites/kummer-etale-morphism), every nonempty open of the fibre product maps onto an open of V̂ meeting the interior, and the boundary is pulled back from X, so the interior of the fibre product is dense.

Descent: on the v-cover of (iii) the given maps agree on the overlaps over S_K; their equaliser on each overlap is closed (Y separated) and contains a dense open by (iv), so it is everything; a closed subdiamond containing all points is the whole diamond (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/isomorphism-criteria-for-v-sheaves-and-stacks), and v-descent of maps into the v-sheaf Y gives the unique descended map (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/diamonds-are-v-sheaves).
acceptance: For the modular curve (G = GL₂, no boundary refinement needed), at a cusp the log affinoid perfectoid objects over X̃_∞ are the perfectoid discs in the variable q^{1/∞} of the Tate-curve tower, and (iii) says the perfectoid cusp discs together with interior affinoid perfectoids v-cover the compactified infinite-level modular curve.
Over the open Shimura variety the comparison reduces to the identification of the pro-étale site of S_K with a site of affinoid perfectoid objects over S^◇_{K^p,∞} (no log structure).

nodes.title: Evaluating the Hodge–Tate torsor on perfectoid test objects over the toroidal tower diamond
nodes.statement: In the situation of toroidal-tower-diamond (S0.general) and HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:comparison: let P_HT ⊆ G_{pet,p} ×^{G^c(ℚ_p)} G^{c,an} be the P^c_μ-reduction of the pro-Kummer-étale G^c(ℚ_p)-torsor over S^tor_{K,Σ} given by the logarithmic Hodge–Tate filtration. For every perfectoid space S with a map S → S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞}, there is a P^{c,an}_μ-torsor P_HT(S) ⊆ G^{c,an} × S, functorial in S and compatible with base change, which étale-locally on S̃ → S is P^{c,an}_μ · g_{S̃} for an element g_{S̃} ∈ G^{c,an}(S̃) unique up to left multiplication by P^{c,an}_μ(S̃); the cocycle p₂^*g · (p₁^*g)⁻¹ ∈ P_μ(S̃ ×_S S̃) describes P_HT(S), and right translation g_{S̃} ↦ g_{S̃}·g by G^{an} carries the embedded reduction P_HT(S) to its translate P_HT(S)·g, inducing an isomorphism of the intrinsic P-torsors. P_HT(S) is the preimage in G^{c,an} × S of the graph of the induced map S → FL_{G^c,μ}^◇ = (P^c_μ\G^c)^{an,◇}. This is the passage from the pro-Kummer-étale site of S^tor_{K,Σ} to the v-site of the diamond that Boxer–Pilloni §4.6.1 presuppose and do not prove; it is proved here from log-to-v-comparison.
hypotheses: (G, X) an arbitrary pure Shimura datum (Boxer–Pilloni §4: axioms SV1–SV3), K = K^pK_p neat, Σ a fixed projective K-admissible cone decomposition, smooth for the base cusp lattice at K; at deeper K^pK′_p ⊆ K the same fan is pulled back with its changed cusp lattice and fs logarithmic Kummer charts, without asserting smoothness of every underlying deeper-level space, F/ℚ_p finite splitting G with E(G, X) ⊆ F; G^c = G/Z_s(G), where Z_s(G) is the largest subtorus of the centre Z(G) which is ℝ-split but contains no ℚ-split subtorus (Boxer–Pilloni §4.1.1; Z_s(G) = 1 in the Hodge-type case).
proofSteps: Tower torsor and central kernel. The canonical local systems W_p imported in HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:comparison/canonical-pro-kummer-realizations are, on S_K, the local systems attached to the p-level tower, and their Kummer-étale extensions are attached to the toroidal tower X̃_∞ of log-to-v-comparison (i) (the extension is unique: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:log-sites/boundary-local-system-extension). Their existence as local systems on S_K for every W ∈ Rep(G^c) is the statement that the arithmetic centre Z(ℚ) ∩ K, hence its closure Z_K, acts trivially on representations of G^c = G/Z_s: its image in (Z/Z_s)(ℚ) is a neat arithmetic subgroup of a torus with equal ℚ- and ℝ-split ranks, hence finite and then trivial (AutomorphicBundles:B0/central-split-quotient, AutomorphicBundles:B0/ineffective-fibre-descent). Hence G_{pet,p} ≅ X̃_∞ ×^{K_p/(K_p ∩ Z_K)} G^c(ℚ_p), which is trivialised over X̃_∞ by its tautological section; the tower is not assumed to be a faithful K_p-torsor (S0/tower-action-kernel).

Frames on log affinoid perfectoid objects. For V log affinoid perfectoid over X̃_∞, the slice X_prokét/V is the pro-étale site of V̂ (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:log-sites/log-perfectoid-basis (3)), and the P^c_μ-reduction P_HT of the now trivial G^{c,an}-torsor (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:comparison/hodge-tate-parabolic-reduction) is étale-locally on V̂ of the form P^{c,an}_μ·g with g ∈ G^c(𝒪(V̂′)), unique up to P^{c,an}_μ on the left. Its class is a map V̂^◇ → FL_{G^c,μ}^◇, functorial in V and compatible on fibre products of log affinoid perfectoid objects (log-perfectoid-basis (1)).

Descent to all perfectoid tests. Over the open Shimura variety these maps are the classes of the Hodge–Tate frames of the same pro-étale torsor, so they agree on the parts of the fibre products lying over S_K. FL is separated, so log-to-v-comparison (iii)–(iv) descends them uniquely to π: S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞} → FL_{G^c,μ}^◇. For a perfectoid S → S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞} put P_HT(S) := (G^{c,an} × S) ×_{FL × S} S along the composite with π; since G^c → P^c_μ\G^c is a smooth P^c_μ-torsor with étale-local sections, P_HT(S) is étale-locally P^{c,an}_μ·g_{S̃}, the cocycle p₂^*g·(p₁^*g)⁻¹ ∈ P^c_μ(S̃ ×_S S̃) describes it, and it is functorial and compatible with base change. No effective descent of analytic torsors along v-covers is needed: maps into the v-sheaf FL^◇ glue by the sheaf property.
Two local frames differ by P_μ on the left. Right translation changes their embedding in the trivial G^c-torsor but preserves the intrinsic torsor through the translated isomorphism.
acceptance: For Hodge-type data with perfect Σ, P_HT(S) is the pullback of the Hodge–Tate torsor along a map S → S^{tor}_{K^p,Σ} of perfectoid spaces (S3 hodge-compactified-period-maps (c)).

nodes.title: Boxer–Pilloni's theorem: the Hodge–Tate period map on the general toroidal tower diamond
nodes.statement: In the situation of kummer-to-v-bridge, the pushed-out coefficient torsor G_{pet,p} is trivial over the toroidal tower diamond S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞} = lim_{K′_p ⊆ K_p} (S^tor_{K^pK′_p,Σ})^◇ (S0.general toroidal-tower-diamond), which gives a K_p-equivariant map of v-sheaves π^tor_HT: S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞} → FL_{G^c,μ} = P^c_μ\G^c (right action), sending a test object S to the class of g_S of kummer-to-v-bridge. The pullback along π^tor_HT of the M^c_μ-torsor U_{P^c_μ}\G^c → FL is M^{an}_HT, and M^{an}_HT ≅ (M^{an}_dR ×^{μ, ℤ_p^×} ℤ_p(1)) ×_{S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ}} S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞}, the pullback from finite level of the canonical extension of the de Rham Levi torsor twisted by the cyclotomic character through μ (Boxer–Pilloni Theorem 4.4.40 in the authors' revised form; the arXiv v1 statement omits the twist, PerfectoidShimuraVarieties/E20). On the open subdiamond S^◇_{K^p,∞}, π^tor_HT restricts to the Hodge–Tate period map, and for Hodge-type data and perfect Σ it is the map of S3 hodge-compactified-period-maps (c). No perfectoidness of the toroidal diamond, no affineness of π^tor_HT and no factorisation through a minimal compactification are asserted for general data.
hypotheses: (G, X) an arbitrary pure Shimura datum (Boxer–Pilloni §4: axioms SV1–SV3), K = K^pK_p neat, Σ a fixed projective K-admissible cone decomposition, smooth for the base cusp lattice at K; at deeper K^pK′_p ⊆ K the same fan is pulled back with its changed cusp lattice and fs logarithmic Kummer charts, without asserting smoothness of every underlying deeper-level space, F/ℚ_p finite splitting G with E(G, X) ⊆ F; G^c = G/Z_s(G), where Z_s(G) is the largest subtorus of the centre Z(G) which is ℝ-split but contains no ℚ-split subtorus (Boxer–Pilloni §4.1.1; Z_s(G) = 1 in the Hodge-type case).
Only K_p acts on the fixed-Σ tower; equivariance for G(ℚ_p) is through the Hecke correspondences of toroidal-hecke-correspondences.

The trivialization over the tower uses kummer-to-v-bridge: the effective deck group, annihilation of the arithmetic central kernel in G^c, and the log-to-v comparison of log-to-v-comparison, whose density part (iv) rests on the recorded openness gap; the tower is not assumed to be a faithful K_p-torsor.
proofSteps: Use kummer-to-v-bridge: the pushed-out G^c coefficient torsor is the effective-deck torsor of the toroidal tower and is trivial over it, the frames of P_HT on log affinoid perfectoid objects give maps to FL^◇, and these descend to S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞} by log-to-v-comparison. The generic finite-level K_p action alone does not supply that trivialization.
Pulling back U_P\G → FL recovers P_HT ×^{P} M = M_HT (definition).

The finite-level logarithmic comparison M_HT ≅ M_dR ×^{μ,ℤ_p^×} ℤ_p(1) with the canonical extension M_dR (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:comparison, Boxer–Pilloni §4.4.38–4.4.39 after Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu Theorem 5.3.1; AutomorphicBundles:B3.general/general-canonical-extension) pulls back to the tower.

Comparison with S3: for Hodge-type data, on the open Shimura variety the logarithmic comparison, hence the Hodge–Tate filtration and P_HT, agrees with Caraiani–Scholze's P_μ-reduction P_p built from the universal abelian variety and its Hodge tensors (Boxer–Pilloni Remark 4.4.39; supplied by T6:comparison/hodge-type-comparison-agreement with its open-locus hypotheses), so π^tor_HT restricted to S^◇_{K^p,∞} is S3 hodge-open-period-map. For perfect Σ, π^tor_HT and the map of S3 hodge-compactified-period-maps (c) agree on the open subdiamond; their equaliser is a closed subdiamond (FL is separated) whose underlying closed set contains the dense subset |S^◇_{K^p,∞}| of |S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞}| = lim |S^tor_{K^pK′_p,Σ}| (the boundary is nowhere dense at each level), so it is everything, and a closed immersion of diamonds that is surjective on points is an isomorphism (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/isomorphism-criteria-for-v-sheaves-and-stacks).
acceptance: For the Siegel datum and any Σ, π^tor_HT is the map of S1 perfectoid-toroidal-siegel-tower composed with the minimal π_HT.
For a datum of non-abelian type (e.g. with an E₇ factor) the map exists although no perfectoid representative of the toroidal tower is known.

nodes.title: Hecke correspondences on toroidal towers with common cone refinements
nodes.statement: In the situation of general-toroidal-period-map, for t ∈ G(ℚ_p) and cone decompositions Σ, Σ′ for which there is a common refinement Σ″ of the pullbacks along the two degeneracy maps (any two admissible cone decompositions have a common refinement; ShimuraCompactifications C3.general), there is a correspondence S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ} ←p₂− S^tor_{K^p(K_p∩tK_pt⁻¹),Σ″} −p₁→ S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ′}, a map of pro-Kummer-étale torsors p₁^*G_{pet,p} → p₂^*G_{pet,p} locally represented by t, and the induced map p₁^*M^{an}_dR → p₂^*M^{an}_dR of étale torsors, compatible with the period maps of the toroidal tower diamonds and, over the tower, with the Hodge–Tate side through M^{an}_HT = M^{an}_dR ×^{μ,ℤ_p^×} ℤ_p(1). Bruhat clause: assume moreover (G, X) of abelian type, G_{ℚ_p} quasi-split, K_p = K_{p,m′,b′} (m′ > 0, m′ ≥ b′ ≥ 0), 0 ≤ m − n ≤ m′ − 1, F large enough as in bruhat-levi-reduction, w ∈ ^MW and t ∈ T(ℚ_p); then over p₂⁻¹((π^tor_{HT,K_p})⁻¹(]C_{w,k}[_{m,n}K_p)) ∩ p₁⁻¹((π^tor_{HT,K_p})⁻¹(]C_{w,k}[_{m,n}K_p)) the map p₁^*M^{an}_dR → p₂^*M^{an}_dR, compared through the reductions M_{dR,m,n,K_p} of bruhat-levi-reduction, is locally represented by the double coset K^c_{p,w,M_μ}M^{1,c}_{μ,m,n}·wtw⁻¹·K^c_{p,w,M_μ}M^{1,c}_{μ,m,n} (Boxer–Pilloni Proposition 4.6.19, Lemma 4.6.20). No single Σ admits all correspondences.
hypotheses: (G, X) an arbitrary pure Shimura datum (Boxer–Pilloni §4: axioms SV1–SV3), K = K^pK_p neat, Σ a fixed projective K-admissible cone decomposition, smooth for the base cusp lattice at K; at deeper K^pK′_p ⊆ K the same fan is pulled back with its changed cusp lattice and fs logarithmic Kummer charts, without asserting smoothness of every underlying deeper-level space, F/ℚ_p finite splitting G with E(G, X) ⊆ F; G^c = G/Z_s(G), where Z_s(G) is the largest subtorus of the centre Z(G) which is ℝ-split but contains no ℚ-split subtorus (Boxer–Pilloni §4.1.1; Z_s(G) = 1 in the Hodge-type case).
Boxer–Pilloni state this for abelian type 'for suitable choices of polyhedral cone decomposition'; the compatibility condition is made explicit here (Σ″ refines both pullbacks).

The Bruhat clause has the hypotheses of bruhat-levi-reduction (abelian type, quasi-split G_{ℚ_p}, K_p = K_{p,m′,b′}, F large), and through it on the tubes and level groups of bruhat-cell-tubes and bruhat-level-groups.

The general correspondence and torsor map use the preceding log-to-v gap. The final Bruhat double-coset clause is conditional on the additional nonsplit Levi-image input recorded below; the source conclusion is retained as a target, not certified by the failed factorization argument.
proofSteps: Construct the correspondence on finite levels with the common refinement (ShimuraCompactifications C3.general) and pass to the diamonds of the towers (S0.general toroidal-tower-diamond, refinement maps are isomorphisms over the open part).

Local sections x₂ = x₁t of the pro-étale torsors give the map of G_{pet,p}-torsors; over the Bruhat domains choose P_HT-trivialisations x′_i with x_i = x′_iwh_i, i.e. x′_i = x_ih_i⁻¹w⁻¹, for h_i ∈ G^{1,c}_{m,n}K^c_p (bruhat-levi-reduction); then x′₂ = x′₁·wh₁th₂⁻¹w⁻¹ with wh₁th₂⁻¹w⁻¹ ∈ P^{an,c}_μ; project to M_μ.

Conditional cancellation argument: put H=wK_p𝒢¹_{m,n}w⁻¹, t′=wtw⁻¹∈T⊆P_μ. If H=(H∩P_μ)(H∩Ū_P)=(H∩Ū_P)(H∩P_μ), P_μ∩Ū_P={1}, and t′ normalises Ū_P, write k=a u and k′=u′ a′. Then kt′k′=at′(t′⁻¹ut′u′)a′ lies in P_μ exactly when u′=t′⁻¹u⁻¹t′; the factors cancel, and need not be separately trivial. Consequently Ht′H∩P_μ=(H∩P_μ)t′(H∩P_μ), and projection to the Levi gives the desired image if Im(H∩P_μ)=K_{p,w,M_μ}M¹_{μ,m,n}. The suggested group theorem explicitly includes t′∈P_μ. In the nonsplit application the two factorisations of H do not follow from a rational Iwahori decomposition: the restriction-of-scalars check in bruhat-level-groups disproves this auxiliary assertion. The source Levi-image equality therefore remains an explicit proof gap; this counterexample does not disprove that equality itself.
acceptance: For GL_2 and t = diag(p, 1) it is the U_p correspondence on the modular tower, with the period map transforming by t on ℙ¹.

For the generic cancellation theorem, t∈P is indispensable: take P={1}, Ū=H=G nontrivial, k=t⁻¹ and k′=1. Its other hypotheses and ktk′∈P hold, but the asserted factorization would force t=1. The Shimura application has t′∈T⊆P.

nodes.title: Auxiliary data for an abelian-type datum: the Hodge-type cover and Lovering's B₁
nodes.statement: Let (G, X) be of abelian type (ShimuraVarieties:V0): there are a Hodge-type datum (G₁, X₁) and a central isogeny G₁^der → G^der inducing (G₁^ad, X₁⁺) ≅ (G^ad, X⁺). Let E be the composite of the reflex fields, T = Res_{E/ℚ}G_m, and (Lovering, §4.6) B₁ = G₁ ×_{G₁^ab} T for the map T → G₁^ab induced by μ_{G₁}, with a datum (B₁, X_{B₁}) and maps (B₁, X_{B₁}) → (G₁, X₁), (B₁, X_{B₁}) → (G, X) (through (B, X_B)) inducing isomorphisms on derived groups or central isogenies, so that all three share the flag variety FL_{G,μ} = FL_{G₁,μ_{G₁}} = FL_{B₁,μ_{B₁}} and the adjoint datum. For a morphism of data g: (H, X_H) → (S, X_S) with H^ad = S^ad, compact opens with g(K′) ⊆ K and Σ for S: S(H)_{K′} → S(S)_K is finite étale, Σ induces a cone decomposition for H with S^tor(H)_{K′,Σ} → S^tor(S)_{K,Σ} finite, and if g(K′) is normal in K the map of neutral components is Galois with finite group Δ(K, K′) = Γ^{ad}_K/Γ^{ad}_{K′}, the action extending to S^{tor,0}(H)_{K′,Σ} with quotient S^{tor,0}(S)_{K,Σ} (Boxer–Pilloni Proposition 4.4.42).
hypotheses: (G, X) of abelian type; neat levels; Σ smooth projective.

This is not the pre-abelian representability argument of S4: it uses the Hodge cover G₁ through a central isogeny of derived groups, Lovering's B₁, Deligne's reconstruction from connected components and finite quotients.

The existing ShimuraVarieties:V0 supplies a lift through a specified central isogeny, not this auxiliary reflex-torus construction. The complete B₁ construction and its maps are separately requested below.
proofSteps: Lovering's construction of B₁ and of the maps (Lovering §4.6, Lemma 3.1.6).

Proposition 4.4.42: over ℂ both neutral components are X⁺ modulo arithmetic subgroups of the common adjoint group, of finite index in one another; rational parabolics correspond under P ↦ g⁻¹(P) (Harris §2.5), giving finiteness on toroidal charts; normality gives the Galois action.
acceptance: For G = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_2 (Hilbert), G₁ = G* is a Hodge-type cover and Δ is the unit group quotient of S5.

nodes.title: Fibre products of torsors and the de Rham torsor of B₁
nodes.statement: (i) Let H₁ → H₂ ← H₃ be smooth affine group schemes over a base S with H₁ → H₂ smooth and surjective (in the application G₁ → G₁^ab and M_{μ_{G₁}} → M^{ab}_μ), P_{H_i} étale torsors and isomorphisms θ₁: P_{H₁} ×^{H₁} H₂ ≅ P_{H₂}, θ₃: P_{H₃} ×^{H₃} H₂ ≅ P_{H₂}. Then P_{H₁} ×_{P_{H₂}} P_{H₃} is an étale (H₁ ×_{H₂} H₃)-torsor (Boxer–Pilloni print P_{H₁} ×_{P_{H₂}} P_{H₁}; PerfectoidShimuraVarieties/E22). (ii) In the situation of abelian-auxiliary-data, for K ⊆ B₁(𝔸_f) and Σ for G₁ there are levels K₁, K₂, K₃ and maps π₁: S^tor(B₁)_{K,Σ} → S^tor(G₁)_{K₁,Σ}, π₂: S^tor(B₁)_{K,Σ} → S(T)_{K₂} over S(G₁^ab)_{K₃}, with M_dR(B₁) ≅ π₁^*M_dR(G₁) ×_{π₃^*M_dR(G₁^ab)} π₂^*M_dR(T) canonically, and likewise for M_HT; with M^c_{μ_{B₁}} = M^c_{μ_{G₁}} ×_{M^{ab,c}_{μ}} T^c, constructions for G₁ extend to B₁ by the trivial construction on the zero-dimensional T-Shimura variety (Principle 4.4.44(1)).
hypotheses: Smooth surjectivity of H₁ → H₂ is needed: flatness of H₁ ×_{H₂} H₃ does not suffice (for H₁ = H₃ = 1, H₂ = G_m and two different trivialisations θ₁, θ₃ of P_{H₂} the fibre product is the equaliser of two sections, not a torsor). It holds for G₁ → G₁^ab (quotient by G₁^der) and for M_{μ_{G₁}} → M^{ab}_μ (surjective because M_{μ_{G₁}} contains the centre).
The compatibility of the c-quotients M^c for B₁ ⊇ Res T is asserted, not proved, in the source; a precise central-character calculation or supplier theorem is still required and is recorded as a gap.
proofSteps: (i) Étale-locally choose sections p₁ of P_{H₁} and p₃ of P_{H₃}; θ₁(p₁) and θ₃(p₃) differ by a section h₂ of H₂, which lifts étale-locally to H₁ because H₁ → H₂ is smooth and surjective; correcting p₁ by the lift gives a section of the fibre product, on which H₁ ×_{H₂} H₃ acts simply transitively.

For (ii), first establish the asserted identity of the coefficient groups and of their Levi quotients after passing to G^c; the auxiliary-datum supplier request records this missing central-character calculation. Given that identity, functoriality gives a morphism of torsors to the fibre product, and the torsor principle in (i) makes it an isomorphism. The group identity does not follow just from the torsor principle.
acceptance: For T trivial (G₁ with G₁^ab = T) the fibre product is M_dR(G₁).

nodes.title: Connected towers of abelian-type data: comparison with the Hodge cover and the descent group Δ
nodes.statement: In the situation of abelian-auxiliary-data: (1) the connected-component towers lim_K S⁰(B₁)_K and lim_K S⁰(G₁)_K are canonically isomorphic, also for minimal and (compatible) toroidal compactifications; (2) for K^p ⊆ B₁(𝔸_f^p) there is (K^p)′ ⊆ G₁(𝔸_f^p) with a finite étale Galois map lim_{K′_p} S⁰(G₁)_{(K^p)′K′_p} → lim_{K_p} S⁰(B₁)_{K^pK_p}; (3) for f: B₁ → G and K ⊆ G(𝔸_f) neat there is K′ with S⁰(B₁)_{K′} → S⁰(G)_K finite étale Galois with group Δ(K, K′), and for K^p there is (K′)^p with lim_{K′_p} S⁰(B₁)_{(K′)^pK′_p} → lim_{K_p} S⁰(G)_{K^pK_p} finite étale Galois; (4) Deligne's reconstruction: S(G, X) = [S⁰(G, X) × 𝒜(G)]/𝒜⁰(G) with 𝒜(G) = G(𝔸_f)/Z(ℚ)⁻ *_{G(ℚ)_+} G^ad(ℚ)⁺ and 𝒜⁰(G) the completion of G^ad(ℚ)⁺ for the congruence topology of G^der(ℚ)_+, the same for minimal compactifications; (5) A⁰(B₁) → A⁰(G) is a continuous surjection whose kernel Δ is profinite, and S⁰(B₁) → S⁰(G) is pro-finite-étale Galois with group Δ; at fixed levels the finite groups Δ(K, K′) of (3) are used, and Δ = lim Δ(K, K′).
hypotheses: (G, X) of abelian type with the data of abelian-auxiliary-data; neat levels.
Over ℂ ≅ ℂ_p from here on, as in Boxer–Pilloni (rationality is not tracked).
proofSteps: (1) Connected components depend only on the connected datum, and (G₁^der, X₁⁺) = (B₁^der, X_{B₁}⁺); the congruence topologies on the adjoint group induced from H(ℚ)_+ and H^der(ℚ)_+ coincide (S0 connected-component-tower).

(2), (3) At fixed tame level choose a first finite Galois map with deck group Δ₁ as in Proposition 4.4.42 and the proof of Theorem 4.4.43, arXiv v1 p. 81. Every deeper Δ_n embeds into this same Δ₁ by compatibility of the arithmetic subgroups. The decreasing images therefore stabilize, proving finiteness of the p-level limit at fixed tame level. Merely having injective maps between finite groups would not give a uniform bound. The limit over all adelic levels in (5) is instead profinite.
(4) Deligne's §2.1 reconstruction (ShimuraVarieties:V6/connected-full-equivalence); the minimal compactification has the same components and the group actions extend by normality.
(5) Mittag-Leffler for the system of finite groups Δ(K, K′); f⁻¹ of congruence subgroups are congruence, and the kernel of G^der(ℚ)_+ → G^ad(ℚ)⁺ is finite.
acceptance: For G of Hodge type with G₁ = G, B₁^der = G^der, so A⁰(B₁) = A⁰(G) and Δ is trivial in (5); (3) reduces to the neutral-component deck groups of S0.

nodes.title: Tilde-limits of connected components, finite quotients and induced towers
nodes.statement: Let (X_i)_{i∈I} be a cofiltered system of separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(C, O_C) with finite transition maps, and X a perfectoid space with X ~ lim_i X_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit), with projections φ_i. (i) Components (Boxer–Pilloni Lemma 4.4.6): if every X_i has a finite set Π_i of connected components and Π := lim_i Π_i, then for e = (e_i) ∈ Π the subset X_e := ⋂_i φ_i⁻¹(X_{i,e_i}) underlies a perfectoid space, on every affinoid perfectoid U ⊆ X the Zariski-closed subspace cut out by the idempotents 1 − ε_i of the open and closed subsets U ∩ φ_i⁻¹(X_{i,e_i}), and X_e ~ lim_i X_{i,e_i}. (ii) Finite quotients (the tilde-limit half of Boxer–Pilloni Lemma 4.4.7): if a finite group Δ acts compatibly on the X_i and on X, and some X_{i₀} has a Δ-stable cover by pregood affinoids (affinoids V whose preimages φ_{i₀}⁻¹(V) are good affinoid perfectoids, PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid), then for i → i₀ the quotients X_i/Δ are adic spaces with finite transition maps, X/Δ is a perfectoid space covered by the φ_{i₀}⁻¹(V)/Δ, and X/Δ ~ lim_i X_i/Δ. (iii) Induction (the step of Boxer–Pilloni Lemma 4.4.50): let H be a profinite group with a decreasing sequence of open normal subgroups H_n, ⋂_n H_n = 1, S ⊆ H a closed subgroup, and (Y_n)_n a tower as above with Y ~ lim_n Y_n perfectoid, S acting compatibly on Y and on each Y_n through S/(S ∩ H_n); put X_n := Y_n ×^{S/(S∩H_n)} (H/H_n), a finite disjoint union of copies of Y_n, and X := Y ×^S H for the right action on Y, with relation (y, h) ∼ (y·s, s⁻¹h). Then X is a perfectoid space, isomorphic to Y × (S\H) after choosing a continuous section σ of H → S\H, and X ~ lim_n X_n, compatibly with the right H-actions. The product carries the action transported through this section, not a trivial action on its Y-factor.
hypotheses: C complete algebraically closed of characteristic 0 (in (ii) |Δ| is invertible, which gives the averaging projector).
In (ii) the Δ-stable pregood cover is a hypothesis; the application supplies it.
proofSteps: (i) Good affinoid perfectoids U = Spa(A, A⁺) pulled back from affinoids U_{i₀} = Spa(A_{i₀}, A_{i₀}⁺) cover X (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/good-affinoid-perfectoid-basis). The idempotents ε_i ∈ A_i of the open and closed subsets X_{i,e_i} ∩ U_i cut out Zariski-closed affinoid perfectoids, and U ∩ X_e = lim_i (U ∩ φ_i⁻¹(X_{i,e_i})) is the Zariski-closed affinoid perfectoid cut out by the ideal generated by the 1 − ε_i (PerfectoidSpaces:P8/limit-of-zariski-closed-embeddings), with A → A_e surjective (strongly Zariski closed: PerfectoidQuotients:Q4/zariski-closed-subsets-are-strongly-zariski-closed). So colim A_{i,e_i} = image of colim A_i is dense in A_e, and |U ∩ X_e| = lim |U_i ∩ X_{i,e_i}|; glue over U (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing).

(ii) The quotients X_i/Δ exist with finite quotient maps (PerfectoidSpaces:P8/rigid-quotient-invariant-cover) and X/Δ is perfectoid with |X/Δ| = |X|/Δ (PerfectoidSpaces:P8/perfectoid-quotient-invariant-cover). The map |X|/Δ → lim_i |X_i|/Δ = lim_i |X_i/Δ| (PerfectoidSpaces:P8/invariant-spectrum-homeomorphism) is bijective because the fibres are finite orbits (a cofiltered limit of non-empty finite sets is non-empty) and open because every Δ-stable open of |X| is a union of preimages of Δ-stable opens of some |X_i|. On a Δ-stable good affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) the projector a ↦ |Δ|⁻¹Σ_δ δ·a maps colim A_i onto colim A_i^Δ, which is therefore dense in A^Δ.

(iii) Inversion transports the pinned continuous section of H → H/S to a section σ of H → S\H. The isomorphism X → Y × (S\H) is [(y,h)] ↦ (y·(hσ(Sh)⁻¹), Sh), with inverse (y,q) ↦ [(y,σ(q))]; hσ(Sh)⁻¹ belongs to S, so the formula respects the induction relation. Perfectoidness follows from PerfectoidSpaces:P6/product-with-profinite-set. The preimage of the copy Y_n·h ⊆ X_n is (Y ×^{S∩H_n} H_n)·h ≅ Y × ((S ∩ H_n)\H_n). For a good affinoid W = Spa(A,A⁺) pulled back from V ⊆ Y_n, W is S ∩ H_n-stable and the preimage of V·h has ring C⁰((S ∩ H_n)\H_n,A). Continuous sections are locally constant modulo every finite quotient on a sufficiently fine clopen partition; finite-level rings are dense in A. Together these facts give density of the corresponding finite-stage locally constant functions. Compactness gives |X| ≅ lim_n |X_n|; conclude by PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-gluing. The left-coset notation is essential when S is not normal.
acceptance: For a single connected component (Π a point) (i) is the identity, and for Δ acting trivially (ii) is the identity.

For the modular curve tower at tame level K^p and H = GL_2(ℤ_p), (iii) with Y the neutral-component tower and S its stabiliser recovers the full perfectoid modular curve from the neutral component when K^p = GL_2(Ẑ^p), where H acts transitively on π₀ through the determinant.

nodes.title: The abelian-type minimal-compactification period map
nodes.statement: Let (G, X) be of abelian type with auxiliary data (G₁, X₁), (B₁, X_{B₁}) (abelian-auxiliary-data), over C = ℂ_p (ℂ ≅ ℂ_p fixed). Then: (1) there is a perfectoid space S̄*(G)_{K^p} ~ lim_{K_p} S*(G)_{K̄^pK_p} (Boxer–Pilloni's image-type compactification, depending on the Siegel embedding of G₁, with finite maps S*_K → S*_{K̄} that are isomorphisms away from the boundary) and the perfectoid space S*(G)_{K^p} = lim_{K_p} S*^◇(G)_{K^pK_p} (genuine minimal compactifications, perfectoid by S4 preabelian-minimal-perfectoid since abelian type is pre-abelian); (2) there is a G(ℚ_p)-equivariant, prime-to-p Hecke-equivariant map π_HT: S*(G)_{K^p} → S̄*(G)_{K^p} → FL_{G,μ}; (3) S̄*(G)_{K^p} → FL_{G,μ} is affinoid: FL_{G,μ} is covered by affinoids whose preimages are good affinoid perfectoid; (4) the maps for B₁, G₁ and G form a commutative diagram over FL_{G,μ} = FL_{G₁} = FL_{B₁}, equivariant for B₁(𝔸_f), G₁(𝔸_f), G(𝔸_f). This is a period-map theorem for abelian-type data, proved by the Hodge cover, Lovering's B₁, Deligne's reconstruction and finite quotients by the stabilized fixed-tame deck group Δ_{K^p}, distinguished from the full adelic profinite Δ; it is not the pre-abelian representability proof of S4, and for pre-abelian data that are not of abelian type no minimal period map is asserted.
hypotheses: (G, X) of abelian type; over ℂ_p.
Finite quotients of tilde-limits use a Δ-invariant cover by pregood affinoids, supplied by affineness of the period map for G₁ and triviality of the Δ-action on FL.
proofSteps: Hodge input: S3 hodge-compactified-period-maps (a), (b) for (G₁, X₁): perfectoid image-compactified and genuine towers, affinoid π_HT, A(G₁)-equivariance.

B₁: each neutral component of S̄*(B₁) is a finite quotient of a neutral component for G₁ (abelian-connected-towers-and-descent-group (2)); connected components of tilde-limits are tilde-limits (tilde-limit-components-and-quotients (i), Boxer–Pilloni Lemma 4.4.6), and finite quotients with an invariant pregood cover are perfectoid tilde-limits (tilde-limit-components-and-quotients (ii), Lemma 4.4.7); induce over the finitely many K_p-orbits on π₀ (S0 connected-component-tower; tilde-limit-components-and-quotients (iii), the induction of Lemma 4.4.50).

π_HT for B₁: (x, a) ↦ π_HT(x)·a on S̄^{*,0}(G₁) × 𝒜(B₁), with 𝒜(B₁) acting on FL on the right through B₁^ad(ℚ_p); it is invariant under (x, a)·h = (xh, h⁻¹a) for h ∈ 𝒜⁰(B₁) because π_HT is right 𝒜⁰(G₁)-equivariant (π_HT(xh)·h⁻¹a = π_HT(x)·a), so it descends to [S̄^{*,0}(G₁) × 𝒜(B₁)]/𝒜⁰(B₁), right 𝒜(B₁)-equivariantly (Lemma 4.4.51, whose left-action notation a·π_HT(x) is read in the right convention of S3 levi-torsor-over-flag-variety).

G: at fixed compatible tame levels, S̄^{*,0}_{K^p}(G) = S̄^{*,0}_{(K′)^p}(B₁)/Δ_{K^p}, where the finite stabilized group of abelian-connected-towers-and-descent-group (3), denoted Δ in the following quotient argument, acts trivially on FL; the B₁ period map is Δ-invariant and affinoid, so preimages of its affinoids give a Δ-stable pregood cover, the quotient is a perfectoid tilde-limit (tilde-limit-components-and-quotients (i), (ii)) and π_HT descends 𝒜⁰(G)-equivariantly, then induces to S̄*(G) (tilde-limit-components-and-quotients (iii); Proposition 4.4.53); compose with S*(G) → S̄*(G).
acceptance: For G = Res_{F/ℚ}GL_2 (Hilbert, abelian type) it recovers on the open part the period map of the arithmetic Hilbert tower descended in PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S5/hilbert-period-and-domain-compatibility (1).
For Hodge-type data it is S3 hodge-compactified-period-maps (a), (b).

nodes.title: The Levi torsor of an abelian-type datum from its Hodge cover
nodes.statement: In the situation of abelian-auxiliary-data, for neat K ⊆ G(𝔸_f), K′ ⊆ B₁(𝔸_f) with f(K′) normal in K and Σ for G: over the neutral toroidal component S^{tor,0}(G)_{K,Σ}, the de Rham Levi torsor M_dR(G, X) is the quotient by Δ(K, K′) of M_dR(B₁) ×^{M^c_{μ_{B₁}}} M^c_{μ_G} over S^{tor,0}(B₁)_{K′,Σ} (after refining Σ so that S^{tor,0}(B₁)_{K′,Σ} → S^{tor,0}(G)_{K,Σ} is finite and generically finite étale with group Δ(K, K′)), and the same holds for M_HT on the towers; with the fibre-product description of torsor-fibre-product this expresses M_HT(G) through M_HT(G₁) and the torus T.
hypotheses: Abelian type; the refinement of Σ is part of the statement (Boxer–Pilloni say 'possibly after refining Σ').
The necessary triviality of boundary inertia on the pushed-out torsor is a separate supplier obligation; generic Galoisness alone is insufficient.
proofSteps: Push out M_dR(B₁) along M^c_{μ_{B₁}} → M^c_{μ_G} (functoriality of the de Rham torsor in data morphisms; AutomorphicBundles:B1/abelian-canonical-principal-bundle).

The finite toroidal map can ramify at boundary strata. Descent of a locally free torsor through its coarse finite quotient requires the logarithmic descent theorem and trivial action of boundary inertia on the pushed-out fibres; it cannot be justified by ordinary finite étale torsor descent on the interior. Import that precise boundary theorem from the recorded request to AutomorphicBundles B3.general / ShimuraCompactifications C3.general, then descend M_dR and use the logarithmic comparison for M_HT.
acceptance: For G of Hodge type with B₁ → G an isomorphism on derived groups and Δ trivial, the statement is the identity of M_dR.

sources.match: The abelian/Hodge formulas for M_HT.

nodes.title: Compatibility of the toroidal and minimal period maps for abelian type
nodes.statement: For (G, X) of abelian type over ℂ_p, the composite S^{tor◇}(G)_{K^p,Σ,∞} → S*(G)_{K^p} → FL_{G,μ} of the toroidal-to-minimal map with the minimal period map of abelian-minimal-period-map equals π^tor_HT of general-toroidal-period-map. Boxer–Pilloni assert this in Theorem 4.4.45 without proof (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties/E23).
hypotheses: Abelian type; Σ fixed; the toroidal tower is only a diamond.
proofSteps: On the open subdiamond both maps are the Hodge–Tate period map of the relative Hodge–Tate filtration: for G₁ by S3 hodge-open-period-map, transported to B₁ and G through torsor-fibre-product and abelian-torsor-descent, compatibly with the descent group Δ.

Uniqueness: let Y := S^{tor◇}(G)_{K^p,Σ,∞}. Because FL is separated, the equaliser Z ⊆ Y of the two maps Y → FL^◇ is a closed subdiamond (pullback of the closed diagonal). |Z| is closed and contains |S^◇(G)_{K^p,∞}|, which is dense in |Y| = lim_{K′_p} |S^tor_{K^pK′_p,Σ}| (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/underlying-topological-space): at each level the boundary is nowhere dense, and the projections from the open limit are surjective (the fibres of the finite étale levels are finite and non-empty). Hence |Z| = |Y|; a closed immersion of diamonds that is surjective on points is bijective on geometric points, hence an isomorphism (DiamondsAndVStacks:D4/isomorphism-criteria-for-v-sheaves-and-stacks), so Z = Y.
acceptance: For Hodge-type data with perfect Σ it is the factorisation in S3 hodge-compactified-period-maps (c).

sources.match: The asserted compatibility (the sentence continues with 'tor of Theorem 4.4.40').

nodes.title: Integral structure of the Levi torsor at hyperspecial-type level
nodes.statement: Assume G_{ℚ_p} quasi-split with a reductive model over 𝒪_F, M^c_μ ⊆ M^{c,an}_μ the corresponding quasi-compact open subgroup, and K_p ⊆ G(ℚ_p) ∩ G(𝒪_F). Then the étale M^{c,an}_μ-torsor M^{an}_dR over S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ} (the canonical extension of the de Rham Levi torsor; general-toroidal-period-map) has a reduction to an étale M^c_μ-torsor M_dR (Boxer–Pilloni Proposition 4.6.3). Over the toroidal tower diamond, M_HT := M_dR ×^{μ,ℤ_p^×} ℤ_p(1) is the M^c_μ-reduction of M^{an}_HT = M^{an}_dR ×^{μ,ℤ_p^×} ℤ_p(1) given by integral trivialisations (the cyclotomic character through μ lands in M^c_μ since μ(ℤ_p^×) ⊆ M_μ(𝒪_F)). The twist by ℤ_p(1) exists only over the tower (ℤ_p(1) is pro-étale, not étale, over S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ}), so the descent to finite level is performed on the untwisted M_dR.
hypotheses: Abelian type (Boxer–Pilloni §4.5–4.6), quasi-split G_{ℚ_p}, F large enough to split G.
The descent uses that the étale torsor M^{an}_dR is already defined at finite level, because pro-étale descent is not effective in general (Remark 4.6.5).
The quotient used to descend the open reduction is by the effective deck group K_p/(Z_{K^p} ∩ K_p). Compatibility of the G^c-torsor with this kernel is proved in kummer-to-v-bridge (first step).
proofSteps: On a perfectoid S over the tower choose integral g_{S̃} ∈ G^c(S̃) (kummer-to-v-bridge); the cocycle p₂^*g_{S̃}·(p₁^*g_{S̃})⁻¹ lies in P^c_μ(S̃ ×_S S̃); its projection to M^c_μ defines a reduction M_HT ⊆ M^{an}_HT over the tower, functorial in S.
Untwist: M_dR := M_HT ×^{μ,ℤ_p^×} ℤ_p(−1) is an open subset of M^{an}_dR ×_{S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ}} S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞}.

Right multiplication by k ∈ K_p ⊆ G(𝒪_F) replaces g_{S̃} by g_{S̃}k and leaves the cocycle unchanged, so this open is K_p-invariant; since |M^{an}_dR| is the quotient of the pullback by K_p, it descends to an open M_dR ⊆ M^{an}_dR. The action map identifies M^c_μ × M_dR with M_dR × M_dR (checked after pullback), and M_dR → S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ} is smooth and surjective on geometric points, so M_dR is an étale torsor.
acceptance: The integral structure is not the one of invariant differentials on an integral model: in the Siegel case (ignoring the centre) M^{an}_dR is the torsor of trivialisations of ω_A, and a differential is integral for M_dR if it lies in the span of the image of the integral Tate module under the Hodge–Tate map (Boxer–Pilloni Remark 4.6.4); for GL_2 at level GL_2(ℤ_p) (ignoring the centre), M_dR is the torsor of generators of the 𝒪⁺-lattice of ω spanned by the Hodge–Tate image of T_pE.

sources.match: The K_p-invariance that makes the integral reduction descend.
The revised manuscript defines the twisted torsor over perfectoid test objects and untwists before descending.
The integral structure is the Hodge–Tate one.

nodes.title: The analytic level groups G_{m,n}, G¹_{m,n} of a reductive 𝒪_F-group and their Iwahori decompositions
nodes.statement: Let F/ℚ_p be finite and G a split reductive group over 𝒪_F with Borel B = TU, opposite Borel B̄ = TŪ and roots Φ = Φ⁺ ⊔ Φ⁻. Write 𝒢 for the quasi-compact adic space attached to G (the generic fibre of its p-adic completion), Iw = ]B_k[_𝒢 for the Iwahori (the tube of the special fibre of B), 𝒰_α ≅ unit ball for the root group of α, 𝒰°_α for the tube of the identity, 𝒰_{α,m} = {|u_α| ≤ |p^m|} and 𝒰°_{α,m} = ⋃_{m′>m} 𝒰_{α,m′}. For m, n ∈ ℚ_{≥0} let 𝒢_{B,m}, 𝒢_{U,m}, 𝒢_{B̄,n}, 𝒢_{Ū,n} be the affinoid subgroups of elements reducing into B, U, B̄, Ū modulo p^m (resp. p^n), 𝒢°_{B,m} = ⋃_{m′>m} 𝒢_{B,m′}, and put 𝒢_{m,n} = 𝒢°_{B,m} ∩ 𝒢_{B̄,n} and 𝒢¹_{m,n} = 𝒢°_{U,m} ∩ 𝒢_{Ū,n}, together with their partial closures (sets of specialisations). Then: (1) all of these are subgroups of 𝒢^{an} (as functors on complete Huber pairs), with 𝒢_{0,0} = Iw; (2) strong Iwahori decomposition: for every ordering of Φ the product map 𝒯 × ∏_i 𝒰*_{α_i} → Iw (with 𝒰*_α = 𝒰_α for α ∈ Φ⁺ and 𝒰°_α for α ∈ Φ⁻) is an isomorphism of analytic adic spaces; (3) for w ∈ W the product map (𝒯 ∩ G′) × ∏_{α ∈ w⁻¹Φ⁺} 𝒰*_α × ∏_{α ∈ w⁻¹Φ⁻} 𝒰*_α → G′ is an isomorphism for G′ = 𝒢_{m,n} and 𝒢¹_{m,n}, where 𝒰*_α = 𝒰_{α,n} for α ∈ Φ⁺ and 𝒰°_{α,m} for α ∈ Φ⁻; (4) for m, k ∈ ℚ_{≥0}, 𝒢_{m,0} normalises 𝒢¹_{m+k,k}; (5) if m ≥ n and K_p ⊆ G(𝒪_F) ∩ 𝒢_{m−n,0}, then K_p normalises 𝒢¹_{m,n}, so K_p𝒢¹_{m,n} = 𝒢¹_{m,n}K_p is a group. An Iwahori decomposition of K_p over ℚ_p does not imply that this product is stable under regrouping the individual split roots relative to P_μ over F; in particular no factorization by its intersections with P_μ and Ū_{P_μ} is asserted.
hypotheses: G split reductive over 𝒪_F (in the Shimura application F splits G_{ℚ_p}, and the parabolic P_μ contains B).
The source leaves the general case of (3) to the reader and proves only G′ = 𝒢_{0,0}; the proof route below supplies the general case.
The analytic depth groups and their normalisation are constructed here for the Bruhat tubes and Levi reductions; the algebraic Bruhat cells are supplied by ShimuraData D3.
proofSteps: (1) 𝒢_{B,m}, 𝒢_{U,m}, 𝒢_{B̄,n}, 𝒢_{Ū,n} are groups since reduction modulo p^m is a homomorphism; intersections and increasing unions of groups are groups; partial closures are groups because their points over (K, K⁺) are the points of the closed-under-specialisation sets over (K, K°) (Boxer–Pilloni Lemma 3.3.14).

(2) Complete G along B_k to a formal group; the product map of formal schemes 𝒯 × ∏ 𝒰*_{α_i} → Iw is an isomorphism on reduced special fibres (T_k × ∏_{α∈Φ⁺} U_{α,k} ≅ B_k), and on tangent spaces at closed points by the Chevalley commutator relations, whose correction terms are strictly higher in the root order; both sides are formally smooth, so it is an isomorphism, and one passes to generic fibres (Boxer–Pilloni Proposition 3.3.4; ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3/big-cell-criteria, ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1/rational-points-root-datum).

(3) For G′ ⊆ Iw decompose g ∈ G′ by (2) as g = t·u⁺·u⁻ with u^± in the products over Φ^±. Since U × T × Ū → G is an open immersion over 𝒪_F (big cell), g reduces into B̄ modulo p^n iff u⁺ ≡ 1 and into B modulo p^{m+} iff u⁻ ≡ 1, coordinatewise: this gives the radii 𝒰_{α,n} (α ∈ Φ⁺) and 𝒰°_{α,m} (α ∈ Φ⁻). For the grouping by w⁻¹Φ^± reorder the factors with the Chevalley commutator formula; its structure constants are integral and the commutator of factors of radii |p^a|, |p^b| has radius |p^{a+b}| (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1/valued-commutator-estimates), so the radius conditions are preserved and uniqueness follows from (2).

(4) Embed G into some GL_r with B = G ∩ B_{GL_r} (a Borel of GL_r fixed by B, by Borel's fixed point theorem on the flag variety of GL_r); there an element of 𝒢¹_{m+k,k} is 1 + p^k X with X in an explicit order Lie_{m,0} of matrices stable under Ad(𝒢_{m,0}), so h(1 + p^kX)h⁻¹ = 1 + p^k Ad(h)X (Boxer–Pilloni Lemma 3.3.18). For rational m,k, pass to a finite ramified extension where their valuations are integral multiples of a uniformizer. The same matrix-order argument uses the ideals with those valuation thresholds and integral commutator constants; descend the inequality on points. Thus the estimate extends from the integer formulation of the source lemma to the rational depths used in §4.6.

(5) Apply (4) with m−n and n: K_p normalises 𝒢¹_{m,n}, and the product of a subgroup with a normalised subgroup is a group. Do not extract separate split-root factors from a ℚ_p-rational element when P_μ is only defined over F. The restriction-of-scalars negative control below shows why that stronger step fails.
acceptance: For G = GL₂, B upper triangular and m = n = 1: 𝒢_{1,1} consists of the integral matrices (a b; c d) with |c| < |p| and |b| ≤ |p|, and 𝒢¹_{1,1} of those with moreover a, d ≡ 1 modulo p^{1+}; for ℚ_p-points this means modulo p².

Each element of H∩P has both lower-left entries zero modulo p²; the same holds in H∩(U_-×1), because its second matrix is the identity. Their products therefore miss (u_-(p),u_-(p))∈H. nodes.title: Tubes of Bruhat cells in the analytic flag variety and their description as orbits
nodes.statement: In the situation of bruhat-level-groups, let P ⊇ B be a parabolic with Levi M, FL = P\G, ^MW the Kostant representatives and, for w ∈ ^MW, U_w ⊆ FL the open translate of the big cell with U_w^{an} ≅ ∏_{α ∈ w⁻¹Φ^{−,M}} 𝒰_α^{an} through (u_α) ↦ w∏_α u_α. Put ]C_{w,k}[ = P\PwIw (the tube of the Bruhat cell C_{w,k} of the special fibre) and, for m, n ∈ ℚ ∪ {−∞}, let ]C_{w,k}[_{m,n} ⊆ U_w^{an} be the image of w∏_{α ∈ w⁻¹Φ^{−,M} ∩ Φ⁻} 𝒰°_{α,m} × ∏_{α ∈ w⁻¹Φ^{−,M} ∩ Φ⁺} 𝒰_{α,n} (images in the sheaf-theoretic sense), together with the partial closures obtained from the closed balls and the specialisation closures. Then: (1) for any ordering of the roots, ∏_{α ∈ w⁻¹Φ^{−,M} ∩ Φ⁺} 𝒰_α × ∏_{α ∈ w⁻¹Φ^{−,M} ∩ Φ⁻} 𝒰°_α → ]C_{w,k}[, (u_α) ↦ w∏ u_α, is an isomorphism; (2) ]C_{w,k}[_{0,0} = ]C_{w,k}[, ]C_{w,k}[_{m,n} = ]C_{w,k}[_{m,0} ∩ ]C_{w,k}[_{0,n} for m, n ≥ 0; (3) orbit description: ]C_{w,k}[_{m,n} = P\Pw𝒢_{m,n} = P\Pw𝒢¹_{m,n} for m, n ∈ ℚ_{≥0}, and likewise for the partial closures; (4) for m ≥ 0, a profinite K_p ⊆ 𝒢_{m,0} and s ≥ 0, ]C_{w,k}[_{m+s,s}K_p is a finite disjoint union of translates ]C_{w,k}[_{m+s,s}h, h ∈ K_p; (5) consequently (P^{an} ∩ wK_p𝒢¹_{m,n}w⁻¹)\wK_p𝒢¹_{m,n}w⁻¹·w = ]C_{w,k}[_{m,n}K_p for K_p ⊆ 𝒢_{m−n,0}.
hypotheses: Hypotheses of bruhat-level-groups; in the Shimura application P = P_μ, FL = FL_{G,μ} and M = M_μ.
In Boxer–Pilloni's application the unipotent radical of P is abelian, so the root groups for w⁻¹Φ^{−,M} commute; in general the order does not matter by the commutation lemma used in the source.
proofSteps: (1) Immediate from the strong Iwahori decomposition (bruhat-level-groups (2)) and P ∩ wIww⁻¹-cancellation: write PwIw = Pw·∏_{α ∈ w⁻¹Φ^{−,M}} 𝒰*_α (Boxer–Pilloni Corollary 3.3.7).
(2) From the definition by radii.

(3) By the Iwahori decomposition of 𝒢_{m,n} for the grouping w⁻¹Φ^± (bruhat-level-groups (3)), w⁻¹Pw ∩ 𝒢_{m,n} absorbs the factors with α ∉ w⁻¹Φ^{−,M}, leaving w∏_{α ∈ w⁻¹Φ^{−,M}} 𝒰*_α with the radii of the definition; the same computation applies to 𝒢¹_{m,n} because the torus and Levi factors are absorbed in P (Boxer–Pilloni Corollary 3.3.17).

(4) For h ∈ K_p, ]C_{w,k}[_{m+s,s}h = P\Pw𝒢¹_{m+s,s}h = P\Pwh𝒢¹_{m+s,s} by (3) and the normalisation bruhat-level-groups (4); two such translates are equal or disjoint, and there are finitely many because 𝒢_{m+s,s} ∩ K_p has finite index in K_p (Boxer–Pilloni Lemma 3.3.19).
(5) K_p normalises 𝒢¹_{m,n} (bruhat-level-groups (4) with K_p ⊆ 𝒢_{m−n,0}), so 𝒢¹_{m,n}K_p = K_p𝒢¹_{m,n}, and (3) gives the stated quotient presentation (Boxer–Pilloni, proof of Proposition 4.6.12).
acceptance: For G = GL₂, P = B, w = 1: ]C_{1,k}[_{m,n} is the disc {|z| < |p^m|} in the chart z of ℙ¹ around the B-fixed point, independent of n.

nodes.title: Reduction of the Levi torsor over Bruhat domains
nodes.statement: Assume G_{ℚ_p} quasi-split with P_μ containing a Borel B over ℚ_p, F/ℚ_p finite splitting G with μ over F, a reductive 𝒪_F-model, and K_p = K_{p,m′,b′} (the preimage of B modulo p^{m′} and of U modulo p^{b′}, m′ > 0, m′ ≥ b′ ≥ 0). For w ∈ ^MW let K_{p,w,M_μ} be the image of wK_pw⁻¹ ∩ P_μ in M_μ (it lies in the Iwahori of M_μ(𝒪_F) and has an Iwahori decomposition N × wT_{b′}w⁻¹ × N̄; Proposition 4.6.9), and for 0 ≤ m − n ≤ m′ − 1 let M¹_{μ,m,n} be the elements of M_μ reducing to U_{M_μ} modulo p^{m+ε} for some ε > 0 (strict valuation greater than m) and to Ū_{M_μ} modulo pⁿ; K_{p,w,M_μ} normalises M¹_{μ,m,n} (Lemma 4.6.11). Then, if F is large enough that the composite Gal(F̄/F) →^{χ_cycl} ℤ_p^× →^{μ} M^{an}_μ factors through K_{p,w,M_μ}M¹_{μ,m,n}, the torsor M_dR has, over (π^tor_{HT,K_p})⁻¹(]C_{w,k}[_{m,n}K_p) ⊆ S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ}, a reduction M_{dR,m,n,K_p} to an étale torsor under K^c_{p,w,M_μ}M^{1,c}_{μ,m,n} (Proposition 4.6.12 in the authors' revised form; arXiv v1 reduces M_HT); these reductions are compatible in (m, n, K_p) (Proposition 4.6.14); for m = n the pushout M_{dR,n,K_p} := M_{dR,n,n,K_p} ×^{K^c_{p,w,M_μ}M^{1,c}_{μ,n,n}} K^c_{p,w,M_μ}M^c_{μ,n} is a torsor under an affinoid group; and for Hodge-type data with perfect Σ, M_{dR,n,K_p} becomes trivial over Spa(R, R⁺) ×_{S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ}} S^tor_{K^pK′_p,Σ} for some K′_p ⊆ K_p, a finite flat cover of any pregood affinoid Spa(R, R⁺) (Proposition 4.6.15 in the revised manuscript).
hypotheses: Abelian type (the truncated period map π^tor_{HT,K_p} of Boxer–Pilloni §4.5 is stated for abelian type), quasi-split G_{ℚ_p}.

The tubes ]C_{w,k}[_{m,n} = P\PwG¹_{m,n} of Bruhat cells, the level groups G¹_{m,n} with their Iwahori decompositions and the normalisation lemma (Boxer–Pilloni §3.3: arXiv v1 Corollary 3.3.14 and Lemma 3.3.15, revised manuscript Corollary 3.3.17 and Lemma 3.3.18) are constructed in bruhat-level-groups and bruhat-cell-tubes; the algebraic cells C_w themselves are ShimuraData:D3/bruhat-integral.
proofSteps: ]C_{w,k}[_{m,n}K_p = (P^{an}_μ ∩ wK_pG¹_{m,n}w⁻¹)\wK_pG¹_{m,n}w⁻¹·w (Boxer–Pilloni Corollary 3.3.14 of arXiv v1; bruhat-cell-tubes (5), using that K_p normalises G¹_{m,n} by bruhat-level-groups (4)).

For perfectoid S over the preimage choose g_{S̃} ∈ wG¹_{m,n}K_p (kummer-to-v-bridge); the cocycle lies in P_μ ∩ wG¹_{m,n}K_pw⁻¹ and its image in M_μ lies in K_{p,w,M_μ}M¹_{μ,m,n} (Lemma 4.6.11 via Proposition 4.6.9's root-group decomposition): a reduction M_{HT,m,n,K_p} of M^{an}_HT over the preimage in the tower, which is K_p-invariant.

Before descending, twist by the cyclotomic character through μ, which factors through K_{p,w,M_μ}M¹_{μ,m,n} by the hypothesis on F: this gives a K_p-invariant reduction M_{dR,m,n,K_p} of M^{an}_dR over the tower (ℤ_p(1) is only pro-étale over the finite level, so the twisted M_{HT,m,n,K_p} itself does not descend).
Descend M_{dR,m,n,K_p} to (π^tor_{HT,K_p})⁻¹(]C_{w,k}[_{m,n}K_p) as in integral-levi-reduction, using that M^{an}_dR is étale at finite level (Remark 4.6.5).
Compatibility and pushout by construction; Proposition 4.6.15 by Elkik approximation of sections of the torsor at finite level.
acceptance: For G = GL_2, w = 1 and K_p = Iwahori, K_{p,1,M_μ} = T(ℤ_p) and the reduction is the torsor of trivialisations of the canonical-subgroup filtration over the ordinary-type domain.
Example 4.6.10: for G_{ℚ_p} = Res_{ℚ_{p²}/ℚ_p}GL_2 the projected group K_{p,1,M_μ} is the image of B(ℤ_p) in T(ℚ_{p²}) × GL_2(ℚ_{p²}), not a product Iwahori.

gaps.title: Openness of the completed log affinoid perfectoid charts over the toroidal tower diamond
gaps.detail: log-to-v-comparison (iv) needs: for W log affinoid perfectoid over the toroidal tower X̃_∞ in the pro-Kummer-étale site of S^tor_{K,Σ}, the map Ŵ^◇ → S^{tor◇}_{K^p,Σ,∞} = lim (S^tor_{K^pK′_p,Σ})^◇ is universally open on underlying spaces (equivalently, the projections V̂^◇ ×_{S^{tor◇}} Ŵ^◇ → V̂^◇ are open). It is a cofiltered limit of composites of Kummer étale maps, which are open (DLLZ), but the fs-versus-adic fibre-product comparison at the boundary and openness in the limit are not written in any source; Boxer–Pilloni Theorem 4.4.40 and §4.6.1 use the resulting descent without comment. With it, the interior is dense in every fibre product and the Hodge–Tate frames descend. The effective deck group, the annihilation of the arithmetic centre in G^c and the v-cover property are planned in S6 and are not part of this gap. S6 owns the statement (RT-AREA-padic-1/4); the natural place for a general version is the logarithmic foundations of HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:log-sites.

gaps.title: Auxiliary reflex-torus datum and coefficient Levi fibre products
gaps.detail: ShimuraData D4/central-isogeny-lift is narrower than Lovering’s B₁ construction. Supply the norm/cocharacter homomorphism from Res_{E/ℚ}G_m, the auxiliary Shimura datum and both maps, their reflex-field and functoriality properties, and the character-lattice proof that passing to G^c preserves the asserted Levi fibre product. The torsor fibre-product principle only proves (i), not these input identities.

gaps.title: Torsor descent through ramified toroidal finite quotients
gaps.detail: S6/abelian-torsor-descent uses a finite map which is Galois on the interior but can ramify at the boundary. Prove logarithmic/coarse quotient descent of the canonical pushed-out Levi torsor, including triviality of each boundary inertia action on its fibres, before asserting a locally free descended torsor. Neither finite Galoisness nor ordinary finite étale descent proves this boundary claim.

gaps.title: The p = 2 truncated-group integral Hodge–Tate estimate for modified formal models
gaps.detail: Pilloni–Stroh Théorème 1.9 proves the bound for p ≥ 3. Remarque 1.10 reports the replacement bound 2 at p = 2 without a written proof. T5/modified-hodge-bundle and T5/modified-minimal-model retain this condition. S3’s threshold n₀ = 2g + 1 and congruence exponent n₀ − 2g are therefore conditional; this does not qualify S1’s independently established all-prime perfectoid representability.

gaps.title: Nonsplit Bruhat-domain Levi image in the local Hecke correspondence
gaps.detail: Prove Boxer–Pilloni Lemma 4.6.20 for quasi-split G_{ℚ_p}, a parabolic P_μ defined over a splitting field F, K_p=K_{p,m′,b′}, 0≤m−n≤m′−1 and t∈T(ℚ_p): Im((wK_p𝒢¹_{m,n}tK_p𝒢¹_{m,n}w⁻¹)∩P_μ→M_μ)=K_{p,w,M_μ}M¹_{μ,m,n}·wtw⁻¹·K_{p,w,M_μ}M¹_{μ,m,n}. Source E41 gives a false separate-vanishing inference. Cancellation proves a conditional group lemma, but the needed P/opposite-unipotent factorization of H=wK_p𝒢¹_{m,n}w⁻¹ fails for the restriction-of-scalars example in bruhat-level-groups. Supply a different Galois-compatible image argument, or state sufficient additional hypotheses and prove the remaining general case separately. No counterexample to the displayed Levi-image equality is claimed.

requests.need: At level K^pΓ(pᵐ) over ℚ for the Siegel datum (K^p contained in a level-N subgroup, N ≥ 3 prime to p): the description of the boundary strata of the minimal compactification X*_{Γ(pᵐ)} and of the map X*_{Γ(pᵐ)} → X*_{Γ₁(pᵐ)} on them through lower-genus Siegel spaces (Faltings–Chai V.2; Pilloni–Stroh Théorème A.11), with the constancy of inertia along each stratum, as used in Scholze, torsion paper, Lemma 3.2.35. The integral minimal and toroidal compactifications at good level are cited from the existing nodes C5/integral-minimal-space, C5/minimal-hodge-ampleness, C5/integral-toroidal-space, C5/valuative-properness and C5/higher-level-toroidal-normalization.

For a Hodge-type datum with a Siegel embedding (G, X) ↪ (G̃, X̃): for a cofinal set of admissible cone decompositions Σ there are Σ̃ and closed immersions S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ} ↪ S̃^tor_{K̃^pK̃_p,Σ̃} for all small K_p, compatible with the level transition maps, the closed immersion of the open Shimura varieties and the maps to the minimal compactifications (Lan, Closed immersions of toroidal compactifications of Shimura varieties, Math. Res. Lett. 29 (2022), Theorem 2.2, as used in Boxer–Pilloni §4.4.25 of the revised manuscript). The existing node C3/level-datum-functoriality and C3.general/general-map-descent give the maps; the request is for the closed-immersion property.

Baily–Borel compactifications Sh*_Γ(G, X⁺) of connected Shimura varieties Γ\X⁺ for every arithmetic Γ ⊆ G(ℚ)_+ (also non-congruence and with torsion), over ℂ: normal projective, finite maps Sh*_{Γ₁} → Sh*_{Γ₂} for Γ₁ ⊆ Γ₂ of finite index, the identification Sh*_{Γ₁}/(Γ₂/Γ₁) ≅ Sh*_{Γ₂} for Γ₁ normal in Γ₂, and the finite maps for G → G^ad sending (G(ℚ)_+ ∩ K)\X⁺ to π(Γ)\X⁺ (Hansen–Johansson, §5.3, Propositions 5.18–5.19).

Connected Shimura data (G, X⁺) (Deligne's conditions on a semisimple G and a G^ad(ℝ)⁺-orbit) with the connected data (G^der, X⁺), (G^ad, X⁺) attached to a Shimura datum, and the pre-abelian notion for connected data: (G, X⁺) is of pre-abelian type if (G^ad, X⁺) ≅ (G̃^ad, X̃⁺) for a Hodge-type datum (Hansen–Johansson Definition 4.1, after Moonen 2.10), agreeing with D4/preabelian-type for full data.

For a closed embedding of Shimura data ι: (G, X) ↪ (G′, X′) and K = K′ ∩ G(𝔸_f): the extension Sh*_K(G, X) → Sh*_{K′}(G′, X′) ⊗ E of the canonical-model map to minimal compactifications is finite, and maps the boundary to the boundary and the interior to the interior (used without reference by Scholze §4.1 and Hansen–Johansson Proposition 5.14).

For Hilbert–Blumenthal abelian varieties with 𝔠-polarization: the 𝒪_F-linearised Weil pairing ẽ_n: A[pⁿ] × A^∨[pⁿ] → 𝔡⁻¹ ⊗ μ_{pⁿ} with e_{pⁿ} = Tr ∘ ẽ_n, and the choice of a generator β of 𝔠𝔡⁻¹(1) with its change-of-choice law (Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams Definitions 5.6–5.7).

The unit group Δ(N) = 𝒪_F^{×,+}/((1 + N𝒪_F)^×)² and the finite étale Δ(N)-torsor from the G*-variety (fixed polarization module) to the arithmetic G-variety, the maps attached to changing 𝔠 by isogenies (Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams Proposition 8.4 and Lemma 8.22).

At finite p-level: the G*, intermediate (G-level with fixed G*-polarization) and arithmetic G Hilbert varieties at levels Γ*(pⁿ), Γ(pⁿ), Γ₀(pⁿ) with the maps β₁, β₂; the level-structure action through γ^∨ = det(γ)γ⁻¹ and the polarization action; the Weil-pairing components (𝒪_F/pⁿ)^× and U_n; the finite torsors under Γ̄₀(p^m, pⁿ), P̄Γ₀(p^m, pⁿ) = Γ̄₀/Z_n (Z_n = (1 + N𝒪_F)^×/(1 + pⁿN𝒪_F)^×), Ē(p^m, pⁿ), Δ(pⁿN) and, on identity components, Δ_n(N) (Birkbeck–Heuer–Williams Lemmas 8.5–8.19, with the corrected stabilisation argument for Δ_n(N) when p = 2).

For F = ℚ: the identification of both Hilbert groups with GL₂ and of the Hilbert moduli and level structures (μ_N-structures on A, Γ(pⁿ)-structures on A^∨) with the modular-curve ones of the full-level modular curves, with the sign conventions of the Weil pairing matched.

For an abelian-type datum and a Hodge-type central derived cover, construct Lovering’s auxiliary B₁ = G₁ ×_{G₁^ab} Res_{E/ℚ}G_m with the specified reflex-norm map, Shimura cocharacter, maps to G₁ and G (through B), and common adjoint flag variety. Prove the compatibility of Z_s, G^c and the Levi fibre-product identity used in S6/torsor-fibre-product; a lift through a fixed central isogeny alone does not supply these statements.

Prove descent of the pushed-out canonical de Rham/Levi torsor under the finite toroidal quotient in Boxer–Pilloni Theorem 4.4.43(5), arXiv v1 pp. 80–81, and Remark 4.6.6, pp. 89–90: identify boundary inertia on compatible toric charts, prove its action on the pushed-out fibres is trivial, and descend as an étale torsor; compare the logarithmic Hodge–Tate torsor. Coordinate the finite ramified quotient hypotheses with ShimuraCompactifications C3.general.

Provide the fully faithful perfectoid-space-to-diamond functor with the analytic base/untilt fixed, so a map between diamonds represented by perfectoid spaces over C lifts uniquely to an analytic morphism. The general analytic diamond-functor statement does not imply full faithfulness for all analytic adic spaces. For S3 also identify maps from a perfectoid space over C to the smooth analytic flag with maps to its diamond on perfectoid tests, using the flag’s actual analytic functor of points; full faithfulness between two perfectoid objects alone does not supply a nonperfectoid target.

Provide the reflex-field representable homogeneous Hodge–Tate flag P_μ\G, the universal parabolic torsor, its Levi quotient U_P\G and associated-bundle universal properties, including analytification and the inversion/opposite-parabolic dictionary. Coordinate with AutomorphicBundles B0. This is the generic interface already requested by the accepted T2/open-tower suppliers; construct it upstream of T2, not in S3.

Import the pure Shimura datum and its morphisms, adjoint and product data, Hodge/abelian-type predicates and central derived-isogeny convention from ShimuraVarieties §P.1; import the Hodge cocharacter class and reflex field from §P.3. These replace the retired ShimuraData D3/D4 nodes listed in its supersededNodes ledger. This is the upstream roadmap contract, not a claim that these carriers exist at the pinned library commits. The adjoint-datum construction alone does not include the injectivity of X → X^ad onto a union of connected components (Milne, Introduction to Shimura varieties, Proposition 5.7(a), p. 55); retain that additional comparison obligation when using the adjoint descent in S4. The ShimuraData accepted retirement ledger already forwards it as an upstream Check.

Import PELModuli §M5.4: for totally real F, the scalar-determinant Hilbert group G*, its polarization trace form and symplectic trace embedding, with the induced map of Shimura data. Keep the full restriction-of-scalars GL₂ group distinct from G*. These replace the retired ShimuraData D5 trace-form and trace-embedding nodes.

Import T2/p-level-tower, T2/tower-right-action and T2/infinite-level-diamond from the accepted whole packet. Require actual supplied canonical models (abelian type through V6/V8); finite transitions, finite étale only at neat open levels; T_(gh)=T_h∘T_g and conjugated levels; spatial compactified and locally spatial open limits over the fixed untilt; and separated quasi-pro-étale projection after strictly totally disconnected perfectoid tests. No general torsor conclusion or perfectoidness is imported. The three former S0 nodes are retired, not parallel constructions.

The toroidal Siegel perfectoid tower is the rigid tilde-limit from Pilloni–Stroh, not the unverified generic fibre of a formal inverse limit.
