Sources checked: ps16 Introduction, Théorème 0.4, PDF p. 2; ps16 Appendice A, Corollaire A.19, PDF p. 30; ps16 Appendice A, opening paragraph, PDF p. 21; bp26 §3.3, p. 34.

The open tower is the boundary complement and the finite-level quotients use the actual effective integral action. The strict Iwahori has diagonal symplectic reduction and is distinct from both Γ₁ and Γ₀. Sources checked: sch15 §3.1, Theorem 3.1.2(i), p. 971; sch15 §3.1, footnote 7, p. 971.

Made the choice of ℤ_p^× lift of the finite residue-unit label explicit. Tate cusp charts distinguish Heuer’s full GL₂ family from the fixed-similitude SL₂ family, with the given lower-unipotent q-root action. Sources checked: heuer20 §1.1, Theorem 1.1, and §3, Lemma 3.4, Proposition 3.8, Theorems 3.17 and 3.22, Proposition 3.20, pp. 2–25; heuer20 §2.2, Definition 2.7, p. 8, and §2.7, p. 15; heuer20 §1.1, p. 1.

The finite Hodge-to-Siegel maps need the small-level closed-immersion condition. Extension to minimal compactifications is finite, and that stronger V8 contract remains requested. Sources checked: sch15 §4.1, first paragraphs and footnote 15, p. 1018; cs17 §2.1, Example 2.1.1 and the following paragraph, p. 11.

The image compactification is kept distinct from its normalization and the genuine minimal compactification. It agrees with the open variety but need not be normal at the boundary. Sources checked: sch15 §4.1, second and third paragraphs and footnote 16, p. 1018; hj25 §5.2, remark after Proposition 5.14, p. 34.

The open Hodge-type tower is obtained inside the Siegel perfectoid construction. It does not consume integral-algebra perfectoidization, which belongs to the genuine minimal argument. Sources checked: cs17 §2.1, Theorem 2.1.2 and footnote 8, pp. 11–12; cs17 §2.1, Theorem 2.1.2, p. 12.

The image-compactified Hodge theorem uses closed-locus tilde-limits and plus-ring completion of those images. It does not silently replace the images by the canonical minimal levels. Sources checked: sch15 §4.1, Theorem 4.1.1 (existence, (i), (ii)) and its proof, pp. 1018–1020; sch15 §4.1, proof of Theorem 4.1.1, p. 1020.

Removing tame-level smallness uses finite invariant perfectoid charts and quotient comparison. The inherited P8 integral-extension/perfectoidization dependency is recorded rather than discharged by neatness. Sources checked: hj25 §5.2, proof of Proposition 5.14, p. 34.

The genuine Hodge minimal tower is a good tower through the finite-tower/integral-extension input. The integral perfectoidization gap remains explicit; this is stronger than the image theorem. Sources checked: hj25 §5.2, Proposition 5.14 with proof, pp. 34–35; bp21 §4.4.27, p. 74.

Arbitrary nonproduct levels use normal compact-open cores and compatible finite quotients. The good-tower conclusions remain conditional on the same finite-tower input as the genuine minimal construction. Sources checked: hj25 §5.2, Corollary 5.15 with proof, p. 35.

Good towers base-change through their actual affinoid ring completions and tilde-limit topology. Replaced a process reference in the acceptance example; its distinction between E_p and C is preserved. Sources checked: hj25 §5.3, conventions, p. 35.

Lifting the genuine-to-image diamond map uses fixed-base/untilt perfectoid full faithfulness. The exact D6 request is retained; full faithfulness between arbitrary analytic adic spaces is not asserted. Sources checked: bp21 §4.4.27, p. 74.

Uniqueness of the canonical infinite-level diamond gives independence of the symplectic embedding. This does not identify the finite image compactifications as normal schemes. Sources checked: cs17 §2.1, Theorem 2.1.3(1), p. 12.

The imported algebraic flag/torsor interface is upstream of T2. Inversion, the lower Siegel parabolic and right quotient are explicit; point quotients in Lean express only the elementary carrier portion. Sources checked: bp21 §4.4.10, Remark 4.4.11, p. 66; bp26 §3.1, p. 33; bp26 §3.3, Remark 3.3.1, p. 35.

Prime-to-p Hecke acts trivially on the flag and compatibly on the tower. Right-action normalization agrees with the GL₂ isogeny and centre tests. Sources checked: sch15 §3.3.3, Theorem 3.3.18(iii)–(iv) with proof, pp. 1012–1014; bp26 §3.3, Remark 3.3.1, p. 35.

Qualified the elliptic acceptance isomorphism by the transported BHW linearization. The intrinsic W-dual identity retains the central-cocharacter Tate twist, which cannot be dropped from the equivariant comparison. Sources checked: sch15 §3.3.3, proof of Theorem 3.3.18(vi), p. 1014; sch15 §3.3.3, Theorem 3.3.18(v)–(vi) with proof, pp. 1013–1015; sch15 §3.3, p. 1003.

The graph factor A+ZC, quotient frame, W-dual multiplier and radius neighbourhood of every integral matrix agree. The denominator-zero matrix tests the Iwahori hypothesis; the genus-one dual convention recovers cz+d. Sources checked: bhw §2.2, Lemma 2.4, p. 8; bhw §2.2, Definition 2.2, p. 8; bhw §3.3, Lemma 3.19 and its proof, p. 13; sch15 §3.3, p. 1008; bp26 §3.3, p. 35.

The T2 open v-sheaf map is evaluated on S2’s perfectoid representative using the actual analytic flag functor of points. The stronger D6 map comparison remains requested separately from perfectoid full faithfulness. Sources checked: cs17 §2.1, Theorem 2.1.3(1), p. 12; cs17 §2.3, after Lemma 2.3.7, p. 21.

The Levi/automorphic pullback is imported from T2, retaining its relative-filtration and representable flag inputs. Its analytic incarnation preserves the cyclotomic torsor twist. Sources checked: cs17 §2.1, Theorem 2.1.3(2), p. 12; bpa §4.4.23, p. 74; bpa §4.4, Remark 4.4.12, p. 69.

Datum functoriality is deduced from the canonical relative filtration and the faithful tensor representation. Siegel embeddings are compared through the common construction rather than chosen point coordinates. Sources checked: cs17 §2.3, Lemma 2.3.7 and the construction of π_HT, pp. 20–21; cs17 §2.3, proof of Lemma 2.3.7, p. 20.

Image, genuine minimal and cofinal perfect toroidal extensions are distinguished. A closed Hodge toroidal embedding is an explicit C3.general contract; arbitrary Hodge fans are not asserted perfectoid. Sources checked: bp21 §4.4.27, p. 74; bpa §4.4.25, p. 75; sch15 §4.1, footnote 16, p. 1018.

The modified formal models assert descent of a proven ample power and the finite congruence exponent. The k=1 strengthening is not inferred, and the p=2 truncated-group estimate remains a separate gap. Sources checked: ps16 §1.19, Théorème 1.22 and Remarques 1.23–1.26, PDF pp. 8–10; ps16 §1.19, Remarque 1.26, PDF p. 10; pil20 §12.9.1, p. 81; bcgp21 §6.2.1, arXiv pp. 144–145; ps16 §1.8, Théorème 1.9 and Remarques 1.10–1.11, p. 5 (author version).

The elliptic quotient-line normalization, chosen Tate section and BHW left level action yield cz+d. The coordinate change Z=-z and γ dual make its relation to the right graph convention explicit. Sources checked: bhw §3.3, formula (3.2), Lemma 3.17, Definition 3.18, Lemma 3.19, Proposition 3.21, Remark 3.23, pp. 12–14; pan22 §3.1.1, sequence (3.1.1), p. 17.

The modular Hodge–Tate exact sequence retains the determinant/Tate line for Hecke equivariance. Pan’s quotient graded piece is gr^0, not gr^1; a chosen trivialization transports the action. Sources checked: pan22 §4.2.3, sequences (4.2.1)–(4.2.3), p. 38; pan22 §4.2.3, p. 38.

The Hilbert flag splits over the field into embedding factors. No integral product identification at ramified p is inferred; the trace pairing and polarization variance remain specified. Sources checked: bhw §5.3, p. 23; bhw §5.4, Remark 5.21, p. 25.

The basis consists of affinoids with good affinoid-perfectoid inverse images and actual finite-level approximations. Rational subdomains preserve the property; the whole flag is not treated as one affine chart. Sources checked: pan22 §3.2.1, pp. 18–19; sch15 §3.1, Theorem 3.1.2(iii), p. 972.

Property P quantifies over every tame minimal tower, with the semisimple convention for connected data. Open-only representability is insufficient, and the categorical predicate states only its supplied-diagram portion. Sources checked: hj25 §5.3, Proposition 5.16 and Definition 5.17, p. 36; hj25 §5.3, Definition 5.17, p. 36.

Neutral-to-full reconstruction uses component stabilizers, finitely many local-group orbits and induced towers. A neutral infinite component need not be open; its perfectoid closed-fibre construction is separate. Sources checked: hj25 §5.3, Proposition 5.16 with proof, pp. 35–36; hj25 §5.3, proof of Proposition 5.16, p. 36.

The adjoint comparison uses semisimple finite-centre data and compatible finite maps, not equality of the two arithmetic level systems. The SU(2,1) central-closure example remains excluded by that false equality. Sources checked: hj25 §5.3, Proposition 5.18 with proof, p. 36; hj25 §5.3, proof of Proposition 5.18, connected case, p. 36.

Added the uniform order bound by the fixed finite quotient Γ/Γ-triple-prime in the normal-core proof. Finiteness of each group separately would not justify a finite inverse-limit deck group. Sources checked: hj25 §5.3, Proposition 5.19 with proof (congruence case), pp. 36–37; hj25 §5.3, proof of Proposition 5.19 (arithmetic case), pp. 37–38.

Pre-abelian minimal representability follows from the Hodge adjoint datum and Property P. It asserts a representing perfectoid diamond, not an automatic genuine-minimal tilde-limit or arbitrary pre-abelian period map. Sources checked: hj25 §5.3, Theorem 5.20 with proof, p. 38; hj25 §1.3, the paragraph after Theorem 1.5, p. 5.

The boundary pulls back as a reduced Zariski-closed locus and is strongly Zariski closed. Hansen–Johansson Corollary 5.21 supplies the stated conclusion, so the inherited missing-proof allegation E15 remains rejected. Sources checked: hj25 §1.3, Theorem 1.5, p. 4; hj25 §5.3, proof of Corollary 5.21, p. 38.

The reflex-field bridge chooses an abstract complex identification only in the permitted cardinality case and then uses base change to arbitrary C. The underlying canonical diamond is independent of that auxiliary identification. Sources checked: hj25 §1.3, Theorem 1.5, p. 4; hj25 §5.3, conventions, p. 35.

The modular comparison fixes the Weil pairing and distinguishes SL₂ fixed-fibre deck degree p^3 from GL₂ full-family degree p^4. The finite-level exceptional pairing fibre is compatible. Sources checked: bhw §2.1, p. 7; bhw §2.1, display (2.1), pp. 7–8; heuer20 §2.1, p. 6.

The cusp chart uses a lower-unipotent coset action, not a quotient by a nonnormal upper-triangular subgroup. Its q-root multiplier and integral b/d period coordinate agree with Heuer. Sources checked: heuer20 §3.4, Proposition 3.19 and Theorem 3.22, pp. 23–25; bhw §3.1, proof of Proposition 3.8, pp. 10–11.

The modular anticanonical radius comparison uses the discrete m bounds actually proved in Proposition 5.18. It does not interpolate to epsilon<=r/c_p at arbitrary r or assume the missing endpoint estimate. Sources checked: bhw §2.2, Lemma 2.4 and Proposition 2.6, pp. 8–9; bhw §2.2, p. 8.

The geometric, intermediate and arithmetic Hilbert towers keep their finite-level moduli and unit torsor contracts. The adjugate left action and the explicit inert-prime component count distinguish them. Sources checked: bhw §8.2, (8.1), p. 33; bhw §8.2.1, Definition 8.8, p. 34.

The mixed contracted product carries the diagonal correction in its period map. The continuous section of ℤ_p^× in O_p^× gives a product after a choice, with the transported action rather than a trivial first factor. Sources checked: bhw §8.4.2, Lemma 8.25, p. 39; bhw §8.2.3, Corollary 8.11, p. 35.

The pairing is unit-valued on the intermediate tower and scales under level and polarization changes as stated. On the arithmetic tower only its class modulo positive global units is defined. Sources checked: bhw §8.4.2, Lemma 8.26, p. 39; bhw §8.2.2, after (8.2), p. 34.

The finite Δ_n→Δ injection is not used. The odd-prime transition argument and bounded orders, and the finite infinite-level kernel at p=2, give the correctly scoped torsors; the Q(sqrt(5)) control is retained. Sources checked: bhw §8.4, Proposition 8.21, pp. 37–38; bhw §8.4, Proposition 8.21(4), p. 38.

The projective level group quotients by the closure of all tame congruence units, not merely positive units. Its effective action and finite-level torsor identities reduce correctly to F=ℚ. Sources checked: bhw §8.4.1, Lemma 8.24 and diagram (8.7), p. 39; bhw §8.3, Definition 8.17, p. 36.

The GL₂(Q_p) action can change the polarization module by the determinant ideal. Restriction to integral units recovers the finite level action, while scalar p changes the module by p². Sources checked: bhw §8.4.1, Lemmas 8.22–8.23, pp. 38–39.

The Hilbert period maps and trivializations descend with the corrected mixed-span formula. T4 radius endpoints and ramified integral-generator qualifications remain inherited rather than silently removed. Sources checked: bhw §8.5, Lemma 8.28, pp. 39–40; bhw §5.3, Proposition 5.18, p. 24; bhw §5.3, proof of Proposition 5.18, p. 24.

At F=ℚ both Hilbert groups, pairing data and unit quotients specialize to the modular tower with the same variance and action conventions. This comparison does not identify unrelated Hilbert polarization components. Sources checked: bhw §5.1.1, Remark 5.5, p. 19.

Replaced the unjustified finite-subcover inference from arbitrary images by the quasicompact-cover property of the actual pro-Kummer-étale site, before lifting points. This proves a finite joint v-cover on each qc target without using the separate openness gap in (iv). Sources checked: bpa §4.4.40, the paragraph before Theorem 4.4.40 and the theorem, p. 80; bpa §4.6.1, p. 90.

The log-to-v comparison provides the effective coefficient torsor on perfectoid test objects, with central-kernel annihilation and density on fibre products stated explicitly. The openness/density portion remains a conditional input, not supplied by T6 alone. Sources checked: bp21 §4.6.1, pp. 87–88.

The general toroidal period map is a map of tower diamonds via the log-to-v bridge. Agreement with the Hodge/Siegel cases and the central-cocharacter Tate twist are preserved; no general toroidal perfectoid carrier is introduced. Sources checked: bp21 §4.4.38–4.4.40, pp. 77–78; bpa §4.4.40, Theorem 4.4.40, p. 80.

Added t-prime in P to the conditional double-coset argument. Removed the claim that split-root regrouping proves the nonsplit case; the local Levi-image statement is now explicitly conditional on its exact new gap. Separate unipotent vanishing remains false. Sources checked: bp21 §4.6.18, Proposition 4.6.19 and Lemma 4.6.20, pp. 94–96; bpa §4.6.18, Proposition 4.6.19 and its proof, pp. 97–98.

The elementary group fibre product has an honest carrier, but the auxiliary Shimura cocharacter, reflex norm and coefficient Levi identities remain the stronger D4 contract and gap. A central-isogeny lift is not substituted for them. Sources checked: bp21 §4.4.41 and Proposition 4.4.42, pp. 78–80.

The torsor fibre-product principle uses smooth surjectivity to align local sections. It proves the torsor assertion only after the coefficient-group fibre-product identity, whose c-quotient compatibility remains an explicit input. Sources checked: bp21 §4.4.42, paragraph before Theorem 4.4.43, p. 80; bp21 Principle 4.4.44, p. 82.

Added the fixed initial finite deck group Δ₁ as a uniform bound at fixed tame level. The full adelic kernel is profinite; it is not made finite by injective maps between varying finite groups. Sources checked: bp21 Theorem 4.4.43, §4.4.48 and Lemma 4.4.52, pp. 80–85; bp21 §4.4.48, p. 83.

Added the pinned continuous-section theorem as a direct prerequisite of induction. The formulas use left cosets S\H, the transported right H-action, good affinoids and finite-quotient density; quotient and component assertions have their actual hypotheses. Sources checked: bp21 §4.4.1, Lemma 4.4.6, p. 64; bp21 §4.4.1, Lemma 4.4.7 with proof, pp. 64–65; bp21 §4.4.48, proof of Lemma 4.4.50, p. 84.

Distinguished the stabilized finite fixed-tame Δ_{K^p} used for quotient perfectoidness from the full adelic profinite Δ. The abelian minimal period map uses the Hodge cover and is not claimed for all pre-abelian data. Sources checked: bp21 Theorem 4.4.45, Lemmas 4.4.50–4.4.52 and Proposition 4.4.53, pp. 82–85; bp21 §4.4.40, p. 78.

The boundary finite quotient is allowed to ramify. Descending the pushed-out Levi torsor retains the exact boundary-inertia/trivial-fibre-action contract; ordinary finite étale descent on the interior is insufficient. Sources checked: bp21 Theorem 4.4.43(5) and Remark 4.6.6, pp. 81, 89–90.

The two maps agree on the dense interior and hence everywhere on the reduced source into the separated flag. The log-chart density input is retained, so the comparison is not justified merely by constructing each map independently. Sources checked: bp21 Theorem 4.4.45, p. 82.

The integral Levi reduction uses the logarithmic comparison with its twist and an actual open compact subgroup. It inherits the log-to-v density input and is not a consequence of the finite-level filtration alone. Sources checked: bp21 §4.6, Proposition 4.6.3 and Remark 4.6.5, pp. 88–89; bpa §4.6.2, proof of Proposition 4.6.3, p. 91; bpa §4.6.2, Remark 4.6.4, pp. 90–91.

Removed the false factorization of a nonsplit rational compact product relative to a splitting-field parabolic. Kept normality/product-group formation, supplied rational-depth matrix-ideal normalization and synchronized strict diagonal depth p^{1+}. Added the restriction-of-scalars counterexample. Sources checked: bpa §3.3.3, Proposition 3.3.4 and its proof, pp. 38–39; bpa §3.3.13, Lemma 3.3.14 and Proposition 3.3.15, p. 41; bpa Lemma 3.3.18 and its proof, p. 42; bpa §3.3.19, the definition before Lemma 3.3.20, p. 43; §4.6.8, p. 92; proof of Proposition 4.6.12, p. 94; proof of Lemma 4.6.20, p. 98; bp21 §3.3, Proposition 3.3.2, Lemma 3.3.11, Proposition 3.3.12 and Lemma 3.3.15, pp. 37–40.

Corrected the base point to [0:1] under the fixed second-row convention. The tube is an open root disc rather than the algebraic cell itself; the orbit and finite-translate formulas use the analytic depth groups. Sources checked: bpa §3.3.6, Corollary 3.3.7, p. 39; bpa §3.3.8, Definition 3.3.10 and Remarks 3.3.11–3.3.12, pp. 39–41; bpa Corollary 3.3.17 and Lemma 3.3.19 with proofs, pp. 42–43; bp21 §3.3, Corollary 3.3.5, Corollary 3.3.14 and Lemma 3.3.16, pp. 38–41.

Corrected the universal positive-epsilon congruence to the existential strict-depth condition. The Levi reduction retains rational-depth normalization, the actual nonsplit projected compact group and cyclotomic containment before descending M_dR. Sources checked: bpa §4.6, Proposition 4.6.12 and its proof, pp. 94–95; bp21 §4.6.8, Proposition 4.6.9 and Example 4.6.10, pp. 90–91.
